name: Laoghaire Buadhach

attributes.attribute: a hero of the Ulster Cycle
died so the poet Aodh would not be killed
the angry king who wanted the poet dead

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Laoghaire Buadhach, the Victorious, was a hero of the Ulster Cycle. He gave his life so that a poet named Aodh would not be slain by the angry king Concobar Mac Nessa. His death was an honor within the warrior code of Ulster.

okr.objective: Present Laoghaire Buadhach as the Ulster hero who died for a poet.
key_results: The source calls him Laoghaire the Victorious.
It says he died rather than let the poet Aodh be killed by the king.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (Checkmark 2008), s.v. Laoghaire Buadhach.
